brief:
Pulitzer Prize-winning historian Benjamin Moser contends that Zionism represents a departure from Judaism rather than an expression of it, according to Zeteo. In an interview, Moser argues the ideology is being deployed to supplant Jewish religious and cultural identity while enabling the oppression and displacement of Palestinians.

Moser's framing challenges the equation of Jewish identity with support for Zionism, positioning the two as fundamentally distinct ideological projects with divergent consequences for both Jewish communities and Palestinian populations.
dek: Pulitzer Prize-winning historian Benjamin Moser makes the case to Mehdi for why Zionism isn't Judaism, and how it is being used to replace Judaism while oppressing and displacing Palestinians.
title: Jewish historian argues Zionism displaces Judaism and Palestinians
